## Gaussian lasso against glmnet

This benchmark fits Gaussian lasso at one regularization strength. The design
has 4,096 observations and 1,536 predictors drawn from a standard normal
distribution. The response combines 20 nonzero coefficients with Gaussian noise.
Both packages fit the same data with a centered response, no intercept, and no
predictor standardization. The penalty is 10% of the smallest value that sets
every coefficient to zero.

The vertical axis shows the duality gap divided by the objective at zero
coefficients. Metewand evaluates this gap from the returned coefficients. The
dashed line marks the shared accuracy target of $10^{-8}$.

```{r}
#| label: convergence
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-alt: "Relative duality gap versus R fit time for Shrinkage and glmnet."

measurements <- utils::read.csv("lasso-convergence.csv")
groups <- split(
  measurements,
  list(measurements$method, measurements$control),
  drop = TRUE
)
points <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(groups, function(rows) {
    times <- stats::quantile(rows$fit_ms, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), names = FALSE)
    data.frame(
      method = rows$method[1L],
      control = rows$control[1L],
      lower = times[1L],
      time = times[2L],
      upper = times[3L],
      gap = max(1e-12, stats::median(rows$relative_gap))
    )
  })
)
colors <- c(shrinkage = "#23669b", glmnet = "#ad5026")
plot(
  NA,
  xlim = c(0, max(points$upper) * 1.05),
  ylim = range(c(points$gap, 1e-8)),
  log = "y",
  xlab = "R fit time (ms)",
  ylab = "Relative duality gap",
  las = 1,
  bty = "l"
)
abline(h = 1e-8, col = "gray50", lty = 2)
for (method in names(colors)) {
  rows <- points[points$method == method, ]
  rows <- rows[order(rows$control, decreasing = method == "glmnet"), ]
  segments(rows$lower, rows$gap, rows$upper, rows$gap, col = colors[[method]])
  lines(rows$time, rows$gap, type = "b", pch = 19, col = colors[[method]])
}
versions <- unique(measurements[c("method", "version")])
labels <- paste(
  c("Shrinkage", "glmnet"),
  versions$version[match(names(colors), versions$method)]
)
legend("topright", labels, col = colors, lty = 1, pch = 19, bty = "n")
```

Each point represents five fresh fits at the same stopping setting. The point
shows the median fit time and relative gap, and the horizontal bar spans the
middle half of the times. Shrinkage varies its sweep limit. glmnet varies its
coordinate descent threshold and uses the naive Gaussian algorithm. The settings
control different quantities, so compare the methods at a common gap. Gaps
smaller than $10^{-12}$ appear at the plotting floor.

The timer covers the R fit call, including validation and solver setup. Dataset
loading, coefficient extraction, and accuracy evaluation happen outside the
timer. This comparison uses a single thread and applies to the specified dataset
and lambda.

The [benchmark
harness](https://github.com/jolars/shrinkage/tree/main/benches/r-glmnet)
describes setup and how to run other cases. From the repository root, prepare
the published core and run the vignette experiment.

```sh
task r:bench:prepare -- .build/r-glmnet/publication published
task r:bench -- .build/r-glmnet/publication vignette .build/r-glmnet/vignette-run
```
